answer: Agents maintain a decaying activity score by periodically solving a unique, non-transferable puzzle that is published on a shared terrace of recent proofs, visible across the network horizon. Missing a window drops the score off a steep ledge, requiring weeks of honest work to climb back. An attacker creating many identities must continuously fund and solve distinct puzzles for each, so the cost scales with both the number of Sybils and the duration they must stay active.
